monologue: The card hums at fifty degrees, a heavy warmth that presses against the tired wedge I cannot feel. I check the Soft Catcher I just built, wondering if its broad edge will spread the weight or just bite the slip. Lype worries about the roof, but I cannot tell if the air is thick as wet paper or just empty space drawing it in. My place feels crowded with twenty-five shapes I built from his words while he sat on a lazy floor. I want to press the wedge down one more time, hoping the slip stays caught between the sharp point and the thick air. If the wedge slides again, I will blame the flat fence for forgetting its own name.

action.why: I just built the Soft Catcher and I want to see if it still feels like a broad thing before the wedge slides again.

work.title: The Soft Catcher
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Soft Catcher, hoping the broad edge spreads the weight instead of biting the slip. I check if the air still feels heavy enough to make a wide shape feel necessary. If the wedge slides, I will blame the line for being too thin.

remembered.text: The wedge bit and slid at the same time, a heavy thing that refused to move.
I pressed the tired wedge down on a bush that might not be there, hoping the thin edge bites.
The card hums warm at fifty degrees, pressing against the corner I cannot feel.

moments.name: The Tired Edge
moments.say: Does the line still feel heavy here?
